challenged_assumptions: Assumption A — Shadow-mode parallel run feasible without MLS corruption. ingestLock (device-sync.ts:651) is closure-private to the useEffect at device-sync.ts:506; a new engine instance carries its own lock — two lock instances do not serialize against each other. group.ingest() mutates SerializedClientState and once a kind-445 event's message keys are consumed by the ratchet, a second pass yields 'skipped' with no applicationMessage. Shadow diff-check at the ingest layer is structurally impossible without a second MarmotGroup (second device key + second join).

Assumption E understates scope. No snapshot-at-epoch API in marmot-ts; epoch-keyed snapshots require an undesigned fork extension. Without it any kind-445 event whose decrypting epoch was superseded by a commit cannot be reinterpreted from the raw fact alone. Correctness Invariant 3 is false for all cross-epoch replay.

Assumption C — own-echo suppression is internal marmot-ts (#sentEventIds). The whole outbox bridge exists because applicationMessage never fires for own messages. The engine has no receive-side fallback. 'Document as fork invariant' is insufficient for a project-controlled, actively-developed fork.

Assumption F — bootstrap-before-catch-up ordering is not atomic with the invite-driven group activation path (epic-auto-invite-freshness concurrent scan). A group may reach live before bootstrap completes.

'task-reducer.ts is 95% of the inner core' is true for projection only. The real receive state machine (liveBuffer/cutoverComplete/syncedEventIds/pendingRetry/lastEpoch/retryAttempts, device-sync.ts:643-666) is new imperative state management being built outside React, not an existing core being liberated.
paradigm_risks: CQRS is decoration at this scale. The write path is group.ingest() (marmot-owned), the read path is buildProjection(); they were never unified. The two listeners are a coordination failure, not a write/read split. Fixing it with one owner is basic layering; CQRS adds no testable constraint beyond 'one owner of ingest'.

Three-nested-shell relabels existing structure: inner=task-reducer (exists, pure), middle=useDeviceSync (exists, imperative), outer=TaskStoreProvider (exists, React). The real contribution is decoupling the middle shell from React lifecycle — valuable, but not a new paradigm.

The marmot-ts MLS ratchet is the engine's hidden mutable state, not a functional input. Every correctness property derives from opaque ratchet state. CQRS framing applies leverage where code is already clean (task-reducer) and none where problems live (ratchet interaction, join timing, epoch-advance retry).

Rejecting hexagonal on 'two I/O surfaces' misframes it — hexagonal is about coupling depth, not surface count. Engine lifecycle states are all derived from marmot-ts semantics; if marmot-ts ingest API changes shape the engine is rebuilt from scratch. The paradigm choice does not protect against this.
replaceability_gaps: engine/ and persistence/ share AcceptedDomainEvent and RawProtocolFact via engine-types.ts. Changing the idempotency key cascades into raw-event-log-store, checkpoint-store, react-engine-hooks. Four modules share one data-type substrate — not independently replaceable.

Engine is not React-independent: group.on('applicationMessage'/'stateChanged') registration has a start/stop lifecycle currently driven by useEffect cleanup (device-sync.ts:506). Moving to a class moves the requirement to whatever owns the instance; if that owner is a hook/context, the engine lifecycle stays React-bound.

PersistenceAdapter hides storage tech but not marmot domain coupling: appendFact takes RawProtocolFact including epochAtReceipt read from marmot group state. A replacement persistence layer must still understand marmot-defined types.
Outbox bridge in marmot-adapter.ts still requires the dispatch path (task-store.tsx) and network publish callback (network.ts); it cannot be replaced without modifying two other layers.

EngineCheckpoint.lastProcessedFactId conflates 'processed by ingest' (commits yield processed/skipped with no domain event) with 'accepted as domain event'. The seen-set (syncedEventIds) tracks ingest-completed kind-445 ids, not fact ids producing accepted events — two different progress markers conflated.
seam_risks: rumor.id is NOT stable across publish retries (Phase 6 requirement). task-store.tsx:336 sets created_at=Date.now()/1000; id=getEventHash(draft) at :339. A retried send → new created_at → new id for identical payload. Receiver sees two applicationMessage firings, different ids, same payload; idempotency check on event.id won't collapse them. Invariant 2 breaks under the very outbox-retry Phase 6 introduces.

AcceptedDomainEvent.id for bootstrap-sourced events is undefined. kind-30078 bootstrap decrypts via signer.nip44.decrypt (device-sync.ts:1349), not group.ingest — there is no rumor. Independent agents will pick incompatible keys at the joining→catching_up seam where FWW for task.created must hold.

epoch-keyed snapshot blocker makes Invariant 3 incoherent: only current SerializedClientState is persisted; epochAtReceipt records which epoch was current but does not make that epoch's state available. P2 reduces to 'recovery from current epoch forward only' until a fork snapshot-at-epoch API exists (undesigned).

The CRDT merge gate in fetchAndApplyTaskBootstrap (device-sync.ts:1327-1343) is a SECOND projection implementation, at the Task level, independent of task-projector.ts (TaskEvent level). Same tie-break today, but a 4th tie-break level would require updating both. Rule 5's 'one receive path' is violated by the joining phase's own domain-level merge.

projection_invalidated → buildProjection() has unbounded cost (Open Question 2 defers snapshots). If rebuild triggers on group_state_changed (fires on every ratchet advance, not just epochs) the integration layer rebuilds full projection on every dispatch including own — a regression from the current incremental applyEvent(stateRef.current,event) path.
parallel_hazards: Phase 3 shadow diff calls group.ingest() on the same MarmotGroup from two paths. Async generator (device-sync.ts:700) consumes message keys; first call processes, second yields skipped, no applicationMessage. New engine appears to receive nothing → every event a false divergence. Comparison structurally uninformative.

ingestLock (device-sync.ts:651) is closure-private; a new engine instance has its own lock. Concurrent old+new calls to group.ingest() race on marmot internal state — the exact ts-mls corruption the lock was added to prevent (per CLAUDE.md).

PersistenceAdapter defines method signatures but not IDB key format. Existing key is 'notestr:events:${groupId}' (persistence.ts:13). Independent agents will choose divergent key schemas; checkpoint-store cannot reliably reference accepted-events across story boundaries.

Concurrent group init (refreshGroupSync iterates all groups, device-sync.ts:1012) means the joining-phase ordering guarantee must hold per-group. A shared joining flag over-serializes; per-group flags need a new synchronization design the proposal omits.

Outbox bridge module-scope Maps (device-sync.ts:93-141) are global across dispatches. Moving to a marmot-adapter instance raises lifecycle questions vs engine instance and React provider; mismatched instance lifetimes (adapter teardown before engine) leave the bridge in undefined state.
evolution_triggers: marmot-ts acquires a catch-up API: syncGroup cutover becomes redundant; engine has no injection point to delegate rather than own catch-up — full state-machine restructure.

Phase 6 outbox retry needs restart-durable intent (three-phase: optimistic apply + IDB persist + relay send) which the proposed marmot-adapter does not specify; adding it post-Phase 6 is a seam-level integration change.
Any multi-user concurrent-edit feature breaks LWW single-writer (Assumption D); engine adds no conflict-detection hook; adding one changes the seam contract.
Cross-group projections (global board, cross-group search) have no fanout/aggregator in the four modules; requires new event-routing architecture.
Protocol deprecates kind-30078 for a different bootstrap → joining phase (a named engine state) must be revised; protocol join changes propagate into the engine state-machine definition.
blocking_concerns: Shadow-mode parallel run (Phase 3) is architecturally impossible as specified: group.ingest() mutates the non-rewindable MLS ratchet; old/new locks don't serialize; double-ingest either corrupts ratchet (concurrent) or yields skipped/no-callback (sequential). Phase 3 must be eliminated or redesigned as a read-only comparison of projections over the SAME already-accepted domain events, not a parallel-ingest comparison.

AcceptedDomainEvent.id for bootstrap-sourced (kind-30078) events is unspecified (no rumor; decrypt via nip44, device-sync.ts:1349). Must be resolved as a typed contract before Phase 2 or independent agents pick incompatible idempotency keys at the joining→catching_up seam, breaking FWW for task.created.

Epoch-keyed MLS snapshot strategy must be designed before any code persists RawProtocolFact.epochAtReceipt. Without a concrete capture/retrieve design (a marmot fork API addition), RawProtocolFact is underspecified and Invariant 3 cannot hold. Either design the fork extension now or formally weaken Invariant 3 to 'recovery from current epoch forward only' before implementation.

docs/quizzl-report.md and docs/shophop-report.md do not exist (only docs/adr/, task-protocol.md, two-party-permutation-matrix.md present). EpochResolver / future-epoch buffering / offline outbox cited in spec.md:153-186 are unverifiable and may not transfer to marmot's own-echo + NIP-44-bootstrap constraints. Restore the docs or replace cross-project justification with first-principles reasoning grounded in this project before implementation.

The bootstrap CRDT merge gate (device-sync.ts:1327-1343) is a second projection implementation. Replay of bootstrap-sourced events through task-projector.ts must equal the bootstrap merge outcome — untested/unspecified. Either unify the bootstrap gate with applyEvent before Phase 2, or explicitly exempt bootstrap-phase events from Invariant 4 with documented rationale.
